3.text: The Chukchee are very much afraid of this disease, since it occurs so often.

4.text: In 1896, while I was travelling on the Upper Anui, all the Chaun people,

5.text: hearing of some cases of the disease on the Wolverine River, fled from the

6.text: whole western part of the Chaun tundra in order to avoid the “spirits seeking

8.text: Of nervous diseases, which are also dreaded and considered “subject to

9.text: shunning,” I may make mention of iteˊyun, akin to epilepsy. Sometimes it

10.text: occurs with the usual fits; sometimes with convulsions or with contraction of

11.text: the muscles, amounting almost to a temporary catalepsy. It lasts for several

12.text: hours, and the patient is unconscious during the whole time; then it gradually

13.text: passes away, but in a few days returns, perhaps in a more violent form.

14.text: Iteˊyun progresses rapidly, and invariably ends in the death of the sufferer.

15.text: Sometimes, however, it lasts for years before the fatal issue.

16.text: Another disease of a like character is iuˊmetun, a kind of violent nervous

17.text: affection, which comes on at night like nightmare. During an attack the

18.text: breath appears shortened, the blood rushes to the face, and sometimes the

19.text: sufferer chokes on the spot. The Chukchee attribute both diseases to special

20.text: spirits, and do not like even to mention their names. A man suddenly afflicted

21.text: with such an illness while travelling, may be almost sure that he will not be

22.text: allowed to enter any house, nor will he be given either fire or warm food.

23.text: The well-known form of Arctic hysteria, which is so widespread among

24.text: the Yukaghir and Lamut women, is very rare among the Chukchee, especially

25.text: among the Reindeer branch of the tribe. This disease develops chiefly in the

26.text: form of an uncontrollable desire to repeat in a loud voice each word spoken

27.text: by somebody else, and to imitate every sudden gesture or action. Even the

28.text: women among the Russianized natives, and Russians, are affected with it to

29.text: a considerable extent, while those of the Chukchee are practically exempt

31.text: Leprosy, so frequent among the Yakut, does not attack the Chukchee,

32.text: who have, however, various kinds of skin-diseases, perhaps on account of their

33.text: filthy habits of living. They often call themselves “the not-washing people”

35.text: The most common of skin-diseases is scabies, which often afflicts whole

36.text: families. The Chukchee pay little attention to it. Scabby people have told

37.text: me, half in joke, that they even find pleasure in spending their spare time

39.text: More uncommon is taˊɪrg̣ɪn, a peculiar disease that increases the pigment

40.text: in the skin, so that the afflicted look like mulattoes. They do not complain

41.text: of any pain, but lose in strength and agility; nor can they endure the hard-

42.text: ships of their former pursuits, though their term of life does not seem to be

43.text: shortened. I met with only five cases of this disease.
